findings.observed: The explanation calls a derivation step A_i, without the formula-metavariable marker used by this source's notation.
findings.finding: The missing marker makes this one occurrence inconsistent with the immediately preceding definition and every subsequent indexed formula in the section.
controlling_evidence: The definition on lines 25-33 introduces every step as !A_i.
The expanded modus-ponens definition on lines 68-81 consistently uses !A_i, !A_j and !A_k.
The omitted marker is confined to the single explanatory occurrence on line 40.

findings.observed: The final sentence of the transitivity proof writes B_i = !A without the formula marker and says every copied occurrence is justified by the same rule as !A_k.
findings.finding: The formula marker is dropped, and 'same rule' is too narrow because the preceding sentence allows !A_k to be an axiom, a member of Gamma, or a result of an inference rule.
controlling_evidence: The earlier occurrence on line 73 and the displayed concatenated derivation use !B_i.
Lines 75-77 explicitly distinguish three possible bases for !A_k: axiomhood, premise membership, and an inference rule.
The concatenation argument needs the copied occurrence of !A to inherit whichever of those three bases justified !A_k.

findings.observed: The compactness proof says that every non-axiom, non-premise step follows from earlier formulas by modus ponens.
findings.finding: That enumeration omits the quantifier rules admitted by the FOL version of the same tagged chapter, so the proof as written only covers its propositional build.
controlling_evidence: OLP-0112 conditionally imports the quantifier-axiom and rule section whenever the FOL tag is active.
OLP-0115 defines two quantifier inference rules and abbreviates either one as QR.
The compactness argument remains valid for every allowed inference rule because restricting Gamma to Gamma_0 preserves the stated freshness conditions.
